posts.name: Shaikh Abdul Mannan
posts.cooked:
First, the most important rule in ERPNext development is to never change the core ERPNext or Frappe files directly. If you do, your changes will be deleted during the next update. That’s why we create a Custom App.

Think of a Custom App like a plugin or a “mod” for a game. It sits on top of the core system, keeping all your special changes safe and separate.

Step 1: Create Your Custom App

This is your personal toolbox where you’ll keep all your code.

  1. Navigate to your bench folder in the terminal.
  2. Run the command you mentioned: bench new-app your_app_name (It’s best to use underscores _ instead of spaces for the app name).

This command creates a new folder inside your-bench-folder/apps/ with all the basic files and folders needed for your app.

Step 2: Add Your Changes

Now, you’ll add your new features or customizations and tell the system to save them inside your new app.
A) If you are creating NEW things (like a new DocType):

  1. Log in to your ERPNext site.
  2. Go to the DocType list and create your new DocType.
  3. In the “Module” field, select the module that belongs to your custom app.
  4. When you save, ERPNext automatically creates the necessary files (.json, .py, .js) for that DocType inside your app’s folder (apps/your_app_name/your_app_name/...).

B) If you are CUSTOMIZING existing things (like adding a field to the “Sales Order” form):

  1. Go to the form you want to change (e.g., “Sales Order”).
  2. Click Menu > Customize.
  3. Add your custom fields or change properties.
  4. After saving your changes, you must export them. Go to the “Customize Form” list, find your customization, and under the Actions menu, select Export Customizations.
  5. In the pop-up, choose your custom app and the module. This saves your changes as a file in your app, so you can move them to the server later.

Step 3: Save Your Code to GitHub

Now that your changes are saved as files in your app’s folder, you need to save that version of the app online. We use Git for this.

  1. In your terminal, go inside your app’s folder: cd apps/your_app_name
  2. Run these commands to save your work:
  • git add . (This prepares all your new files)
  • git commit -m "My awesome new feature" (This saves a snapshot of your changes with a message)
  • git push (This uploads your saved changes to your GitHub repository)

Step 4: Deploy on Your Server

This is the process of getting your saved code from GitHub and making it live on your server.

  1. Get the App: On your server’s bench, run this command to download your app from GitHub: bench get-app https://github.com/your-username/your-repo-link.git
  2. Install the App: Tell your specific site to use the app: bench --site your_site_name install-app your_app_name
  3. Apply the Changes (Migrate): This is the final and most important step. It reads all the changes from your app’s files and applies them to the site’s database. bench --site your_site_name migrate

The migrate command makes permanent changes to your database. Always test your app on a development site before deploying and running migrate on a live production site!
